_what: The README's first screen, above `Driftproof **consumes**` (spec 126). Its words are written here once, the title (the operator's descriptor of 1 Oct 2026) among them; scripts/build-readme-opening.mjs composes them into README.md with every other value read from the file it names: the two plugin lines from the README's own Install section, the Node.js major from package.json engines.node, the anchors from the README's own headings, the report count from docs/data/stats.json, and the latest finding from the newest report's plain summary (docs/data/report-summaries.json). Spec 020 AC-30 and spec 126 read the README against this file. Never edit the README's opening by hand.
title: Driftproof (driftproofhq): open-source agent skill evaluation and regression testing across model releases
pitch: Does your AI coding skill really help, and does the help survive a new model? Driftproof measures it and gives you a receipt.
what: A skill is a `SKILL.md` file that teaches an AI coding agent how you like things done. Driftproof runs your skill's own test tasks with the skill and without it, has a model score every answer several times, and tells you whether the skill clearly helps, clearly hurts, makes no clear difference, or whether there were too few answers to tell. Each result is a receipt: a file with the numbers that anyone can check. Run it again when a new model comes out.
try_heading: Try it in Claude Code, no API key
commands: `/driftproof:init` sets up a skill with example tests, and `/driftproof:run` measures a skill in your repository and writes its receipt. It runs on your Claude Code subscription. You need Node.js {node_major} or later.
badge_caption: live badge for the bundled example, generated from its own receipt.
